route_role_definitions.Core: Scheduled first-trip anchor. A defined external blocker must name the fallback.
route_role_definitions.Strong: High-value scheduled stop with a clear drop-first position under fatigue or friction.

route_role_definitions.Skip: Intentionally omitted from this route; never rendered as a mandatory stop.

A.title: Temporal Arbitrage Master
A.operating_architecture: Protect scarce openings and first-trip anchors, then spend optional budget only after recovery is funded.

decisions: Run Ferry Plaza / Latine Makers opening window; keep evening lights only if family energy supports it.
Use the first practical Muir reservation; Battery is valid only if parking and wind are frictionless.
Alcatraz first practical slot; use cable car as transport/experience, not an added detour.

recovery: Aquarium late window protects the Monterey overnight transfer
decisions: If light or energy is poor, defer 17-Mile to its legal sunrise/sunset window and skip Bixby.

recovery: arrival-day Valley layer; no checklist after long transfer
decisions: Choose the Wawona/south reveal only when fire, smoke, and access support it; otherwise use the safer current corridor.
Glacier/Washburn require open road, useful visibility, and safe weather; otherwise run Valley fallback.

recovery: final Yosemite morning, then SF arrival recovery first
decisions: Never trade the final Yosemite morning for a forced SF photo stop.
Tea Garden opens first; Twin Peaks only when visibility justifies the climb.
Use Lands End or the family’s favorite neighborhood as the low-regret finale.

B.title: Awe & Light
B.operating_architecture: Protect every Core stop and move discretionary time toward dawn, golden hour, scale, and clean legal viewpoints.

decisions: Ferry and Exploratorium remain the weather-proof spine; lights are a short visual coda.
Early bridge and first practical Muir slot; Battery only with clean wind, parking, and visibility.
Dense Wharf stops yield first when the light or family energy is better spent elsewhere.
Bixby is a drive-through view only; no illegal stop or U-turn.
Use the current safe corridor if smoke, fire, or access degrades the south reveal.
Do the high-country light window only with road and visibility confirmation.
Protect the final Valley light and allow an easy SF arrival.
Twin Peaks belongs only to a clear, low-wind evening.
Coastal light wins over adding another dense neighborhood stop.

C.title: Family Serenity
C.operating_architecture: Protect the Core first, make nap and sensory recovery visible, and drop nonessential friction before comfort breaks.

recovery: long hotel recovery and early night
decisions: Ferry and Exploratorium are the full day; lights are cancelled at the first fatigue signal.
No Battery; use stroller-friendly or low-demand layers after Muir.

recovery: snack, transit reset, and early return
decisions: No Coit, Lombard, Pier 39, Musée, or Ghirardelli; use drop-first order explicitly.

recovery: stroller-compatible Point Lobos segment and late Aquarium
decisions: Keep the coastal drive simple; no Bixby stop and no extra loop after Aquarium.
Valley-only fallback if transfer or children’s energy runs long; never protect Mariposa over Valley.

recovery: long afternoon nap and easy Valley reprise
decisions: Glacier only when conditions are obviously good; otherwise stay in the simple Valley layer.
Drop-first is all discretionary SF viewing after Yosemite.
Tea Garden is carrier-first; use interior Academy recovery if paths or weather are difficult.
Keep the final day intentionally low-demand; no forced add-ons.

D.title: City Texture + Nature Contrast
D.operating_architecture: Keep the natural Core intact, then trade novelty for lived-in Chinatown, North Beach, and a deliberate Golden Gate Park cluster.

decisions: Use the opening market and Exploratorium as a calm city introduction.
Nature anchors stay; Battery is a friction-controlled add-on.
Chinatown includes Dragon Gate, Grant, Stockton, Portsmouth Square, and food/street texture—not only the factory.
Use Bixby only as safe legal drive-through contrast; no scenic shoulder behavior.
Keep natural Core intact but do not force Mariposa or a southern detour.
High-country access and visibility gate the layer.
Return to the city gently; the contrast works only if arrival is not rushed.
After the Oct 3–4 event pressure, cluster Tea Garden + Academy + Botanical in one park day.
Prefer real neighborhood texture to another checklist viewpoint.

E.title: 2026 Event Edge
E.operating_architecture: Use trip-date-specific opportunities only when they improve the family day; the trip remains excellent when an event is declined.

decisions: Exploit Oct 3 Ferry/Latine timing; protect the first day from late arrival debt.
Do not chase the Oct 3–4 park event pressure; keep a robust nature/interior counter-plan.
Use pre-Fleet-Week cable-car timing; Monday Exploratorium closure is already avoided.
Event-edge route still obeys safe Highway 1 and one-night Monterey constraints.
No event benefit justifies a fire/smoke/access gamble in Yosemite.
Weather/access gate high-country stops exactly as in the other routes.
Fleet Week pressure is a reason to avoid a forced waterfront return, not to erase the Yosemite morning.
One controlled Fleet Week encounter only if weather, crowd, noise, and children justify it; otherwise use the park/interior plan.
Cancel an event encounter immediately when family friction rises; the route remains complete without the air show.
